$comment: WHERE EACH SURFACE LIVES. This one file is the answer to 'which domain is the site on'. Changing the site from a free host to a real domain is an edit to this file and nothing else - no HTML, no build script, no link. That is the whole design goal, and it exists because 139 pages carry root-absolute links that only resolve when a surface is served at the root of its own hostname.
$why: Measured, not assumed. 96 pages in edencosmetic and 43 in talorkaradi reference /icon.svg and /products/... . The files those names resolve to live inside each microsite's own directory, so the links are CORRECT and the DEPLOYMENT is wrong. Rewriting the links would bake whatever host they are on into the markup, and all 139 would break again on the next move. A hostname per surface fixes them without touching a single line of the site.
$modeValues: 'free-host' = Cloudflare Pages *.pages.dev, free forever, no domain to buy. 'custom' = a domain you own. Nothing else in this repository branches on the difference.

cloudflare.$comment: The account ID is an identifier, not a secret (it appears in every dashboard URL), so it lives here. The API token IS a secret: it lives only in the repository secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions), never in a file or a chat. Token permission: Account -> Cloudflare Pages -> Edit.

surfaces.name: lab
surfaces.role: AILGEN Lab: the studio's private workbench for every free Workers AI model. Never linked from a site, noindex, its routes behind LAB_PASSCODE.
surfaces.label: AILGEN Lab
surfaces.$secrets: Repository secrets copied to the Pages project on each deploy (tools/site-switch.mjs). LAB_PASSCODE: any password the owner chooses; until it exists the lab answers 423 and stays locked.
surfaces.$kvIds: A KV namespace id per binding, filled in once and committed. It is an identifier, not a secret - the same category as cloudflare.accountId above - and it is already written into cloud/lab/wrangler.toml on every machine that deploys. Declaring it here means tools/site-switch.mjs binds without calling the API, so the deploy needs no Workers KV Storage permission and cannot silently ship a lab with no budget ceiling. Measured reason: binding by lookup made every deploy depend on that permission, the repository token does not have it, and the deploy printed 'KV LEDGER not bound' while continuing - which left gateBudget() returning null and no paid call checked against the ceiling. Until an id is here the API lookup remains the fallback, and the deploy log names this field as the fix that does not involve the token.
surfaces.$budget: The lab's money: paid models (and free ones once the daily allocation is spent, when the owner allows it) go through the AI Gateway LAB_GATEWAY with Unified Billing, paid from prepaid credits. The KV namespace LEDGER records each call's cost (cloud/lab/ledger.js); LAB_BUDGET_USD is the starting budget, changed later from the lab.

$interim: Until a hostname exists, edencosmetic and talorkaradi are published on GitHub Pages at a path, and their root-absolute links 404. tools/link-audit.mjs counts those as 'root-assumed' and exits 0, because they are not defects - they are correct links waiting for the layout to catch up. The audit becomes a real failure the moment a hostname is attached, which is exactly when it should.
$exclude: Build inputs that live beside a surface but are not pages of it (the concatenated src/ fragments and build.sh). Published, their relative links would be dead links: link-audit found 43 of them and nothing else.
